main_text.p: dem dicit, locū hunc latißime patēre. Nā tertiā philosophiæ partem, quæ à Græcis ἠθικὴ, à nobis Moralis appellari potest, cōplectitur: in quā præclara philosophorum ingenia, à Socrate primùm defudarunt, & eam uarijs copiosisq; disputationibus explicarunt. Sed noster Cicero, qui & ipse uarijs in libris, præsertim uerò de Officijs, oratorio more copiosè tractauit: nunc quasi honorarius arbiter, eam in hæc pauca, in quæ intuεatur orator, capita conclusit.

Est igitur uis uirtutis duplex: aut enim scientia cernitur uirtus, aut actione. Nam quæ prudētia, quæ calliditas, quæq; grauissimo nomine sapientia appellatur, hæc scientia poslet una. quæ uerò moderandis cupiditatibus, regendisq; animi motib. laudatur, eius est munus in agendo, cui temperantiæ nomen est. Atq; illa prudentia in suis reb. domestica, in publicis ciuilis appellari solet. Tēperātia autē in suas itidē res, & in cōmunes distributa est, duobusq; modis in rebus cōmodis discernitur: & ea quæ absunt, non expetendo: & ab

page.notes: Left margin shows only fragments of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. The last word "ab" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment placed at the right; it is kept in the text. Several words in the running text are uncertain due to the scan quality, notably "intuεatur" (probably intueatur) and "poslet".
